_about: SERIES SHELF of the Sacred Books of the East (Clarendon Press, Oxford, 1879-1910, ed. F. Max Müller), the Victorian scholars' fifty-volume library of Asian scripture in English. Lane C already holds Müller's Upanishads and Dhammapada (muller), Palmer's Qur'an (palmer) and Legge's Chinese volumes (legge); this shelf takes the rest. Round 62 holds the Buddhist and Jain volumes: Rhys Davids's Buddhist Suttas (1881) and Questions of King Milinda (1890-94), Rhys Davids and Oldenberg's Vinaya Texts (3 vols, 1881-85), Beal's Fo-sho-hing-tsan-king (1883), Kern's Lotus Sutra (1884), Jacobi's Jaina Sutras (1884, 1895) and Buddhist Mahayana Texts (Cowell, Müller, Takakusu, 1894). Round 63 adds the Zoroastrian and Hindu law volumes: Darmesteter's and Mills's Zend-Avesta (3 vols, 1880-87), West's Pahlavi Texts (5 vols, 1880-97), Bühler's Sacred Laws of the Aryas (2 vols, 1879-82) and Laws of Manu (1886), Jolly's Institutes of Vishnu (1880) and Minor Law-Books (1889), Telang's Bhagavadgita (1882) and Oldenberg's Grihya-sutras (2 vols, 1886-92). Round 64 adds the Vedic and Vedanta volumes: Eggeling's Satapatha-Brahmana (5 vols, 1882-1900), Müller's and Oldenberg's Vedic Hymns (1891, 1897), Bloomfield's Hymns of the Atharva-Veda (1897) and Thibaut's Vedanta-Sutras (3 vols, 1890-1904). Original Clarendon printings only: Motilal Banarsidass reprints of the same volumes (1960s on) were spotted by their front matter and refused. Each title gates on its own translator. US public domain. Added 2026-10-17 by lane C (rounds 62-64); Adam may veto. No uids minted.
